sources.title: Wolfes, Helmuth, 1901-1971
sources.creator: Library of Congress
sources.publication: Library of Congress Name Authority File (LCNAF)
sources.researchNote: The GND identifies him as a conductor and composer, born 22 April 1901 in Hanover and deceased 4 September 1971 in Cleveland, Ohio; it records Germany and the United States and identifies the United States as his place of exile. Its variant forms are Wolfes, Helmut Ernst and Wolfes, Helmuth. The heading is taken from the Library of Congress, which spells the forename Helmuth; the German form Helmut, under which he worked before emigration, remains the display name.

sources.shortCitation: Karamu Performing Arts Theatre, on its musicals and operas
sources.fullCitation: Karamu Performing Arts Theatre, Cleveland. “History: Musicals and Operas.” Google Arts and Culture. Records that Benno Frank served as director of musical productions from 1948 to 1967 and Helmuth Wolfes as musical director from 1954 to 1967, the two collaborating on more than thirty-five productions, and that in 1963 the theatre’s opera company was the first group outside New York invited to the New York Summer Festival in Central Park.
sources.title: History: Musicals and Operas
sources.creator: Karamu Performing Arts Theatre
sources.researchNote: The page documents the American half of his working life: thirteen seasons as musical director of the Cleveland theatre founded for interracial performance, in partnership with another émigré from Germany. The accompanying image is titled only “History: Musicals and Operas”, its maker is given as unknown, and it is not stated to portray him, so it is not taken as a likeness.

personNameVariants.publicNote: Form used in the United States and adopted as the heading by the Library of Congress, beside the German spelling under which he worked before the emigration.
